title: Python get data from IPFS error HTTPError: 405 Client Error: Method Not Allowed for url
q_body: I try to get data from IPFS by using ipfs-api . I upload file to IPFS and get CID to put in the code like this. import ipfsApi api = ipfsApi.Client('127.0.0.1', 5001) print(api) api.cat('QmbFMke1KXqnYyBBWxB74N4c5SBnJMVAiMNRcGu6x1AwQH') It's show error like this. HTTPError: 405 Client Error: Method Not Allowed for url: http://127.0.0.1:5001/api/v0/cat?stream-channels=true&encoding=json&arg=QmbFMke1KXqnYyBBWxB74N4c5SBnJMVAiMNRcGu6x1AwQH How to fix it?

title: How do I drop specific NaN values while keeping others based on a pattern of NaNs in the dataframe in Pandas?
q_body: I have a dataframe like this: The pattern it follows is that if the first n rows of Column A are populated, then the next n rows will be "populated" (populated cells could have NaN values as well, but I call them "populated" because I'd like to keep those) for Column B i.e. rows 'n+1' to '2n'. And Column C will have the next n rows i.e. '2n+1' to '3n' "populated", and so on for the rest of the columns. So in the above example, Column A has the first 3 cells populated, Column B has the next 3 cells (cells 4 to 6) populated, and Column C has the next 3 cells after that (cells 7 to 9) populated. Important: When certain cells for a column are populated, the corresponding cells in the same rows will be empty for ALL other columns. After this pattern continues for all columns, it loops back and Column A is populated again, in this case it's 4 cells that are populated this time. So the next 4 cells of Column B are what I want to keep and the next next 4 cells of column C are what I want to keep. Ending up with a dataframe like this: Initially, I tried dropping all NaN cells but realized that NaN cells that I wanted to keep got dropped too. Then I thought of dropping just the NaN cells that are not in between 2 non-NaN cells but the NaN cells I want to keep won't necessarily be between two non-NaN cells like in the example. I guess the only way I can think of is counting the non-NaN values in column A (say it's x number of rows that are non-NaN) and then dropping the first x rows from Column B, first 2x rows from Column C, first 3x rows from Column D and so on.
